text:
Elaine: FYI - ran an nsys sweep after the kernel-selector tweak and I'm seeing a clear H2D spike that's correlating with tail latency in the serving path. attaching a qdrep link (internal) and a tiny timeline screenshot. p50 up ~25% on a small load.

Mike: Can you paste the exact nsys CLI and the filters you used?

Elaine: ran this:
```
nsys profile --output=h2d_sweep --trace=cuda,memcpy,nvtx --sample=none --force-overwrite \
  -- ./redwood_serve --workload=mlbench --batching=dynamic --seq=1024
```
I filtered for "Memcpy H2D" and grouped by thread. The timeline shows frequent ~1.1-1.3ms H2D memcpy events that happen synchronously right before kernel launches.

Ravi: Do the events show `cudaHostRegister` or `cudaHostAlloc` anywhere? If not, that's the driver staging pageable->pinned on-demand which can stall.

Elaine: no hostregs in the trace. Also saw repeated small peer copies (GPU->GPU) around KV cache eviction times; kvcache seems to evict whole chunks, which then cause D2H/H2D churn.

Irene: this smells like pageable allocations getting staged by the driver. If your app writes into pageable host buffers then cudaMemcpyAsync may block the stream while the driver pins pages behind the scenes.

Zach: note that the recent kernel-selector fallback (commit a1b2c3f) introduced a path that uses host staging when seq > 512 to avoid a regressor in small-seq throughput. That might be the regression trigger.

perf-bot: Perf alert: master@a1b2c3f increased microbench "serve-h2d" p50 by 18% vs baseline (automated detection).

Mike: Quick diagnostics:
- repro with `--seq 1024 --batch 1` to hit the fallback path.
- run nsys with `--trace=memcpy,cuda,nvtx,osrt` and open qdrep. Filter for memcpy H2D and look for long gaps between `cudaLaunchKernel` and memcpy start.

Elaine: I ran a quick experiment: enabled a pinned host pool (cudaHostAlloc pool) for staging buffers. Results: H2D memcpy avg dropped from ~1.2ms -> ~0.15ms, tail improved drastically.

Ravi: Nice. But pinned memory has host RAM cost. Suggest LRU pinned pool with a soft cap and fallback to pageable when memory high. Also change batching heuristic: when batch_size > 32 prefer keeping KV pages resident on GPU (avoid D2H/H2D) or split batches.

Irene: Also check peer-to-peer: if GPUs are NVLink-connected, route KV transfers GPU->GPU instead of D2H/H2D. Verify topology with `nvidia-smi topo -m`. And enable `cudaDeviceEnablePeerAccess` early.

Zach: Reproducer idea:
- checkout @ a1b2c3f
- run: `./redwood_serve --seq 1024 --batching=dynamic --kv-shards=2` under nsys as above
- observe high Memcpy H2D/driver pinned activity

Mike: small NVTX suggestion: annotate KV cache read/write and allocator boundaries so we can correlate CPU page-fault pin-time with GPU memcpy start.

Elaine: I'll draft a PR to add a pinned staging allocator with env var to cap it (REDWOOD_PINNED_POOL_MB). Plan: default off for now, enable in Dedicated and Private for customers with memory headroom. Also add an opt-in KV config to prefer GPU-resident reads.

Ravi: +1. Also add a metric to Console: "host_staging_time_ms" per request so we can monitor production.

Irene: One more thing: verify whether the fallback path uses synchronous memcpy vs async. If sync, that serializes CPU/GPU and kills concurrency.

Elaine: Verified: fallback currently uses `cudaMemcpy` (sync) in that branch. Plan change -> `cudaMemcpyAsync` into pinned pool + stream fence, or avoid path entirely.

Zach: I'll own a quick patch to the kernel selector to avoid host-staging for seq in [513, 2048] unless memory signals force it.

perf-bot: Note: Add regression test that runs `serve-h2d` microbench in CI with seq=1024 and assert p50 < baseline*1.1

Mike: tl;dr: root cause = driver-on-demand staging of pageable host buffers triggered by selector fallback + kvcache eviction pattern -> causes H2D stalls. Fix = pinned pool + selector tweak + P2P route + batching adjustments.

Elaine: Thanks all — I'll open PRs for pinned pool and selector guardrails, include before/after nsys qdrep and perf numbers. :trophy:

Mike: LGTM, please @mention infra for memory policy review.

Ravi: Thanks, this explains the perf regression we saw in nightly.

Irene: great work, very actionable.

Zach: thanks, will follow up with selector PR link.

Elaine: closing loop once PRs merged. :white_check_mark:
